orgReasonsEvidence.recurs: 1,646 lessons on disk (720 published, 692 draft, 234 in review: npm run company -- status, 2026-10-25); lane S plans 100 published lessons per two-week cycle (company/ops/projects.json lane-single-card basis).
orgReasonsEvidence.too-big-for-one-context: 14 curricula (content/curriculum/*.json) and 8,260 claims awaiting the fact-checker (company status, 2026-10-25). One lesson fits one context (system3-meta research/bench6/BENCH6.md); the catalogue does not. Held as data for one pooled category-curator, not as 51 manager roles (F-50).
orgReasonsEvidence.independent-checking: Builders never mark their own claims verified (CLAUDE.md; tools/company.mjs claimGates refuses a claim verified by its builder). M6: the independent fact-checker found real errors in 7 of 10 lessons after the builders' own checks passed (system3-meta research/bench6/PREDICTIONS.md). Learner data and a child-safety trigger need a privacy gate (AMD-015).
orgReasonsEvidence.long-horizon: A live product with accounts, a feed and 21 production releases since 2026-10-14 (company/ops/releases.json); the disk is the memory (CLAUDE.md).

sizeReason: 47 roles (46 agent roles plus the founder) run by 32 agent definitions, against the default of 8; at most 10 sessions at once (8 typical), falling by 2 to 3 definitions on 2026-11-23. The category is the unit of scale (F-53, company/decisions/2026-10-25-founder-f53.md): 14 category owners are 14 logical roles on ONE agent definition (category-owner), because the catalogue recurs at 100 lessons a cycle across 14 curricula with their own charters, rulings and routes (sensitive, safety, copyright), which one pooled prompt did not hold (0 of 173 category items closed under the pool, F-53 section 1b); a new category adds one owner and its data, not an agent. The rest: the steps of the two production flows plus the referee owner (builder, interaction-designer, tester (qa-tester plus accessibility-reviewer on one agent), fact-checker, learner-evaluator, pedagogy-critic, route-reviewer, release-manager, design-lead, evaluation-steward), because the constitution separates maker from checker at four gates and the witnesses are never grouped; the category lead and 3 managers who hold priority and lane budgets (head-of-product, portfolio-manager, plus lane M's design-lead above); the operator and its auditor; 7 engineers and stewards of a live product with learner accounts and a privacy gate; 2 for learning and metrics; 1 research pool; personalization-engineer and its independent judge personalization-eval, plus growth-designer. Dated: head-of-strategic-initiatives and vp-marketing park on 2026-11-23, rnd-lead if F-49 is declined (F-52). Further groupings (F53-9: design, eng-review, hq-tools, learner-data, planning, insight) would bring the definitions to about 26 and are the founder's open choice.

baseline.weighed: Benchmark 6 ran the single-agent baseline on this company's work: one vanilla agent (V) with the company's CLAUDE.md, hooks and tools against the many-stage flow (M) on the same 3 cs.systems one-card briefs, scored blind.
baseline.result: V cost $7.19 against $16.66 (43%; about 51% counting its unpriced nested sessions), took 36.5 min against 98, had 0 confirmed S1/S2 defects against 1, 3/3 accepted against 2/3, and won 2 of 3 pairwise. V checked its claims with nested checker sessions it launched itself, which the protocol does not count as independent.
baseline.conclusion: At the size of one lesson the single agent won. The org is kept only for what one agent cannot hold or must not do: the recurring catalogue, the breadth of 14 curricula, and checks independent of the maker (enforced in code, not briefed by the builder). Each item's own flow should look like V: one warm maker running its own checks, then independent checks once (PRINCIPLES.md P2).
baseline.caveats: n = 3 lessons, one model, both arms in parallel on 4 CPUs; M's time includes environment and founder waits.
